Vyasa.description: The legendary sage and author of the Mahabharata, also known as Krishna-Dwaipayana.

Bhima.description: The second Pandava, known for his immense strength and appetite, also called Bhimasena and Vrikodara.

Arjuna.description: The third Pandava and unparalleled archer, considered an incarnation of the divine sage Nara and often referred to by his mother's name, Pritha.

Nakula.description: The fourth Pandava, son of Madri, who adopted the alias Granthika while in disguise at Virata's court.

Sahadeva.description: The youngest Pandava, known for his wisdom, who used the alias Tantripal as a keeper of cattle during the Pandavas' incognito exile.

Kunti.description: The mother of the Pandavas and wife of Pandu, also known by her birth name Pritha.

Draupadi.description: The common wife of the five Pandavas, born from fire; she is also called Krishna and Yajnaseni, used the alias Sairindhri while in disguise, and is identified as the divine form of Sree.

Bhishma.description: The grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, son of Shantanu and Ganga, known for his vow of celibacy and wisdom.

Dhritarashtra.description: The blind king of Hastinapura, father of the Kauravas, and uncle to the Pandavas.

Duryodhana.description: The eldest of the Kauravas and main antagonist to the Pandavas, known for his jealousy and ambition.

Vidura.description: Half-brother to Dhritarashtra and Pandu, a wise minister and advisor in the Kuru court.

Drona.description: The martial preceptor of both the Pandavas and Kauravas, a master of advanced weaponry and warfare; his son is Ashvatthama.

Karna.description: A great warrior, son of Kunti and the sun god Surya, raised by a charioteer; a close friend of Duryodhana.

Drupada.description: King of Panchala, father of Draupadi and Dhrishtadyumna, and an ally of the Pandavas.

Dhrishtadyumna.description: Son of Drupada, born from fire, prophesied to slay Drona.

Subhadra.description: Sister of Krishna and Balarama, and wife of Arjuna; mother of Abhimanyu.

Abhimanyu.description: Son of Arjuna and Subhadra, a heroic young warrior in the epic.

Agni.description: The Vedic god of fire, invoked in rituals and central to many mythological events, including the burning of the Khandava forest.

Indra.description: The king of the gods and father of Arjuna, known by various titles such as Sakra and Purandara.

Takshaka.description: A powerful Naga (serpent) king and friend of Indra, who dwells in the Khandava forest.

Maya.description: A Danava (demon) architect who is saved by Arjuna and Krishna during the burning of Khandava forest.

Ulupi.description: A Naga princess who marries Arjuna during his exile.

Mandapala.description: A sage who, after death, is reborn as a bird to have offspring and fulfill his duties.

Jarita.description: Wife of Mandapala in his bird form, mother of his children.

Sunda and Upasunda.description: Two powerful Asura brothers who gained boons and were ultimately destroyed by their mutual conflict over Tilottama.

Tilottama.description: A celestial nymph created by the gods to cause discord between Sunda and Upasunda.

Narada.description: A divine sage and messenger, known for his wisdom and ability to travel between worlds.

Satyaki.description: A prominent Yadava warrior and loyal ally of the Pandavas, also known as Yuyudhana.

Satyavati.description: Mother of Vyasa, grandmother of Pandu, Dhritarashtra, and Vidura.

Pandu.description: Father of the Pandavas, former king of Hastinapura, who retires to the forest due to a curse.

Madri.description: Second wife of Pandu, mother of Nakula and Sahadeva.

Khandava.description: A forest that is the site of a great conflagration set by Agni with the help of Krishna and Arjuna.

Indraprastha.description: The capital city built by the Pandavas, renowned for its beauty and prosperity.

Hastinapura.description: The ancestral capital of the Kuru dynasty, ruled by Dhritarashtra.

Panchala.description: A kingdom ruled by Drupada, father of Draupadi, and its people, allies of the Pandavas.

Raivataka.description: A mountain where festivals and gatherings of the Vrishnis and Andhakas take place.

Dwaraka.description: The city ruled by Krishna and the Yadavas.

Kuru.description: The dynasty to which both the Pandavas and Kauravas belong.

Andhaka.description: A Yadava clan allied with Krishna, destroyed in the carnage.

Bhoja.description: A clan of Yadavas, some of whom fought for the Kauravas.

Gandiva.description: The celestial bow given to Arjuna by Varuna, renowned for its power.

Kaumodaki.description: The divine mace given to Krishna by Varuna.

Khandavaprastha.description: The original name of Indraprastha, the city given to the Pandavas.

Pushkara.description: A sacred region where Arjuna spends part of his exile.

Manipura.description: A kingdom where Arjuna marries Chitrangada.

Mahendra.description: A sacred mountain mentioned in Arjuna's travels.

Agastya.description: A sage and a sacred spot visited by Arjuna.

Bhrigu.description: A great sage and progenitor of a Brahmin lineage.

Soma.description: The moon god, also associated with the sacred Soma plant and drink.

Varuna.description: The Vedic god of water, who gives Arjuna celestial weapons.

Vayu.description: The wind god, father of Bhima.

Yama.description: The god of death and justice, father of Yudhishthira.

Kaurava.description: Collective term for the sons of Dhritarashtra, the royal family of Hastinapura, including the Pandavas and Kauravas.

Pandava.description: Collective term for the sons of Pandu.

Kauravya.description: A Naga king, father of Ulupi.

Naga.description: A race of serpent beings in Hindu mythology, sometimes involved in the war.

Rakshasa.description: A class of demons or man-eaters in Hindu mythology.

Pisacha.description: A class of flesh-eating demons in Hindu mythology.

Yaksha.description: A class of nature-spirits, often associated with wealth and treasures.

Gandharva.description: Celestial musicians and warriors in Hindu mythology.

Swayamvara.description: An ancient practice where a princess chooses her husband from among assembled suitors.

Jatugriha.description: The 'house of lac,' a palace built to kill the Pandavas by burning.

Kshatriya.description: The warrior and ruler class in the traditional Hindu social order.

Brahmana.description: The priestly class in the Hindu social order, responsible for rituals and learning.

Vaisya.description: The merchant and agricultural class in the Hindu social order.

Sudra.description: The laborer and service class in the Hindu social order.

Brahmacharin.description: A celibate student, the first stage of life in the traditional Hindu ashrama system.

Vanaprastha.description: The forest-dweller stage of life, where one retires from worldly duties.

Yajna.description: A Vedic ritual sacrifice involving offerings to the gods.

Agnihotra.description: A Vedic fire ritual performed as an offering to Agni, the fire god.

Arghya.description: A ritual offering of water, often used to honor guests or deities.

Rishi.description: A sage or seer in Hindu tradition, often credited with composing hymns of the Vedas.

Apsara.description: Celestial nymphs or dancers in Hindu mythology.

Asura.description: A class of powerful beings or demons often opposed to the gods (Devas) in Hindu mythology.

Deva.description: A god or celestial being in Hindu mythology.

Pitris.description: The ancestral spirits or forefathers in Hindu belief.

Dharma.description: Righteousness, duty, or the moral law governing individual conduct.

Adhyatma.description: Spiritual knowledge or the supreme spirit; often refers to the inner self.

Mantra.description: A sacred utterance, sound, or phrase believed to have spiritual power.

Parva.description: A book or section within the Mahabharata; also means 'festival' or 'episode.'

Yuga.description: An epoch or era within Hindu cosmology; there are four yugas in a cycle.

Ratha.description: A chariot, especially one used in battle.

Atiratha.description: A warrior of the highest rank, capable of fighting many opponents simultaneously; a great chariot-warrior.

Sastra.description: A weapon, or more generally, a treatise or scripture.

Sraddha.description: A ritual performed for the ancestors, involving offerings to the Pitris.

Akshauhini.description: An ancient Indian military formation consisting of a specific number of chariots, elephants, cavalry, and infantry.

Suta.description: A caste of charioteers and bards, also refers to Karna's foster family.

Yajamana.description: The sponsor or performer of a Vedic sacrifice.

Upanishad.description: Philosophical texts that form the theoretical basis for Hinduism, exploring the nature of reality and the self.

Anga.description: A limb or part; in Vedic context, refers to auxiliary sciences or limbs of the Vedas.

Veda.description: The most ancient and sacred scriptures of Hinduism, regarded as the source of knowledge and ritual.

Kavi.description: A poet or sage; often used for wise or learned men.

Sannyasa.description: The renunciate stage of life, marked by renunciation of worldly ties.

Samsara.description: The cycle of birth, death, and rebirth in Hindu philosophy.

Moksha.description: Liberation from the cycle of birth and death; spiritual emancipation.

Rajasuya.description: A royal consecration sacrifice performed by ancient Indian kings.

Santi.description: Peace; also the name of a major parva (book) in the Mahabharata.

Aisika.description: A section of the Mahabharata, also called Sauptika-parva, about the night massacre; also refers to a type of weapon or missile.

Brahmacharya.description: The stage of life devoted to celibacy and learning; also means celibacy.

Sruti.description: That which is heard; refers to the Vedic scriptures.

Kripa.description: Royal preceptor and warrior, present during the dice game.

Gandhari.description: Queen of Hastinapura, wife of Dhritarashtra, mother of the Kauravas, warns against the destruction of the family.

Dhaumya.description: Priest and advisor to the Pandavas, accompanies them into exile.

Vikarna.description: One of the Kauravas, who protests Draupadi's humiliation and argues that she was not won fairly.

Sanjaya.description: Charioteer and advisor to Dhritarashtra, narrator of events.

Somadatta.description: An elder Kuru prince, present in the assembly.

Pratikamin.description: A Suta (charioteer) who is sent to bring Draupadi to the assembly.

Kuntibhoja.description: King and relative of the Pandavas, mentioned as an ally.

Hastinapore.description: Capital city of the Kuru kingdom, seat of Dhritarashtra's court.

Sabha.description: Assembly hall or court, specifically refers to the hall where the dice game takes place.

Gandhara.description: Kingdom ruled by Sakuni, located in the northwest of ancient India.

Vahlikas.description: Proper noun, a clan or kingdom allied with the Kurus.

Kusa grass.description: A sacred grass used in Vedic rituals, symbolizing purity.

Ajatasatru.description: Another name for Yudhishthira, meaning 'one without enemies', the eldest Pandava known for his righteousness.

Jayadratha.description: King of Sindhu, antagonist who abducts Draupadi during the Pandavas' exile.

Markandeya.description: Ancient sage renowned for his longevity and wisdom; narrates many stories to the Pandavas.

Surya.description: The sun god, father of Karna, who bestows him with divine armor and earrings.

Vibhishana.description: Brother of Ravana, ally of Rama in the Ramayana, referenced here as a wise counselor.

Hanuman.description: Monkey-god, son of Vayu, brother of Bhima, and devotee of Rama; appears to Bhima in the forest.

Savitri.description: Legendary princess famed for her devotion and cleverness, who wins back her husband Satyavan from Yama.

Satyavan.description: Husband of Savitri, whose life is restored by her devotion and wisdom.

Rama.description: The elder brother of Krishna, often referred to simply as Rama in the context of the Yadava lineage.

Lakshmana.description: Brother of Rama, loyal companion in exile, referenced in stories.

Ravana.description: Ten-headed king of Lanka, abductor of Sita in the Ramayana.

Sita.description: Wife of Rama, symbol of chastity and virtue, abducted by Ravana.

Dwaitavana.description: A forest where the Pandavas resided during part of their exile.

Kamyaka.description: A forest region where the Pandavas spent much of their exile.

Draupadi-Harana Parva.description: The section of the Mahabharata recounting the abduction of Draupadi.

Ghosha-Yatra Parva.description: The section describing the Kauravas' cattle-inspection expedition and their humiliation by the Gandharvas.

Dwaita lake.description: The lake where the Yaksha tests the Pandavas.

Lanka.description: Capital city of Ravana in the Ramayana.

Saraswati.description: The Hindu goddess of knowledge, music, and arts, invoked for wisdom and eloquence.

Janamejaya.description: A king of the Kuru dynasty, great-grandson of Arjuna, to whom the Mahabharata is recited.

Virata.description: The king of the Matsya kingdom, who shelters the Pandavas during their incognito exile.

Kanka.description: The eldest Pandava king who used the alias Kanka while in disguise and is sometimes referred to as Jaya or the son of Ruru.

Sudeshna.description: Queen of Virata, wife of King Virata, whom Draupadi serves as a Sairindhri.

Indrasena.description: A charioteer associated with the Pandavas.

Durga.description: The supreme goddess, invoked and praised by Yudhishthira for protection and victory.

Kichaka.description: Commander of Virata's forces and Sudeshna's brother, who attempts to molest Draupadi and is killed by Bhima.

Satyabhama.description: Wife of Krishna, whom Draupadi claims to have served.

Manmatha.description: The god of love (Kamadeva) in Hindu mythology.

Jayanta.description: One of the names used by the Pandavas in disguise.

Jayatsena.description: One of the names used by the Pandavas in disguise.

Jayatvala.description: One of the names used by the Pandavas in disguise.

Kansa.description: A tyrant king, maternal uncle of Krishna, slain by Krishna; mentioned in Durga's praise.

Nanda.description: Foster-father of Krishna, referenced in Durga's praise.

Vasuki.description: King of the Nagas (serpent beings), whose sister Arjuna marries.

Airavata.description: The celestial white elephant, vehicle of Indra.

Ruru.description: A sage; here, 'Ruru's son' refers to Yudhishthira.

Padma.description: Consort of Narayana (Vishnu), also known as Lakshmi.

Mahishasura.description: A powerful demon slain by the goddess Durga.

Bharata.description: A term for the descendants of King Bharata; here refers to the Pandavas and their lineage, the Kuru dynasty.

Trinavindu.description: A sage whose grace is said to protect the Pandavas.

Jimuta.description: A renowned wrestler defeated and killed by Bhima.

Uttara.description: Son of Virata, prince of Matsya, who drives Arjuna's chariot in battle.

Sikhandin.description: A Panchala warrior born as a woman (Sikhandini) and later transformed into a man, instrumental in the fall of Bhishma.

Vivingsati.description: A Kaurava prince, brother of Duryodhana.

Dussaha.description: A Kaurava prince, brother of Duryodhana.

Chitrasena.description: A Kaurava prince, slain in battle.

Durmukha.description: A Kaurava prince, brother of Duryodhana.

Trigartas.description: A group of allied kings, enemies of Virata and the Pandavas.

Susarman.description: King of the Trigartas, enemy of Virata.

Sukanya.description: Wife of the sage Chyavana, known for her devotion.

Jatasura.description: A rakshasa (demon) who abducted Draupadi and was slain by Bhima.

Akrura.description: A Yadava chief, uncle of Krishna.

Samva.description: A son of Krishna who was involved in the later history of the Yadava clan.

Saivya.description: A king allied with the Pandavas.

Kasi.description: King of Kasi, an ally of the Pandavas.

Vasumanas.description: A king of ancient times, mentioned among celestial observers.

Valaksha.description: A king of ancient times, mentioned among celestial observers.

Supratarddana.description: A king of ancient times, mentioned among celestial observers.

Ashtaka.description: A king of ancient times, mentioned among celestial observers.

Sivi.description: A legendary king, known for his generosity.

Yayati.description: A legendary king, ancestor of the Pandavas and Kauravas.

Nahusha.description: A legendary king, ancestor of the Pandavas and Kauravas.

Gaya.description: A king of ancient times, mentioned among celestial observers.

Manu.description: The progenitor of mankind in Hindu mythology.

Puru.description: An ancestor of the Kuru dynasty.

Raghu.description: A legendary king, ancestor of Rama.

Bhanu.description: A king of ancient times, mentioned among celestial observers.

Krisaswa.description: A king of ancient times, mentioned among celestial observers.

Sagara.description: A legendary king, ancestor of Bhagiratha.

Nala.description: A king known for his story with Damayanti.

Prajapati.description: The lord of creatures, a creator deity.

Kuvera.description: The god of wealth in Hindu mythology, also known by the name Vaisravana.

Tumburu.description: A prominent Gandharva or celestial musician known for his skill in music.

Rohini.description: A celestial maiden, sometimes associated with the moon or as a consort of Vasudeva.

Viswakarma.description: The divine architect of the gods.

Virata Parva.description: The fourth book of the Mahabharata, describing the Pandavas' year of incognito exile in the kingdom of Virata.

Pandava-Pravesa Parva.description: A sub-section of the Virata Parva, detailing the Pandavas' entry into Virata's kingdom.

Matsya.description: The kingdom ruled by King Virata, where the Pandavas spend their incognito year.

Chedi.description: An ancient Indian kingdom, ruled by King Shishupala.

Surasena.description: An ancient Indian kingdom, associated with the Yadavas.

Pattachchara.description: A region or country mentioned near the Kuru kingdom.

Dasarna.description: A kingdom in central India, often allied with the Pandavas.

Navarashtra.description: A region or country mentioned near the Kuru kingdom.

Malla.description: An ancient kingdom or tribe in India.

Salva.description: An ancient Indian kingdom, sometimes associated with the Yadavas.

Yugandhara.description: A region or country mentioned near the Kuru kingdom.

Saurashtra.description: A region in western India, part of modern Gujarat.

Avanti.description: An ancient kingdom in central India, with its capital at Ujjain.

Kuntirashtra.description: The kingdom associated with Kunti, mother of the Pandavas.

Kurukshetra.description: The battlefield where the great war of the Mahabharata takes place.

Himavat.description: The Himalaya mountains, personified as a deity.

Vindhya.description: A mountain range in central India, considered sacred.

Kali.description: A fierce form of the goddess Durga, associated with destruction and power.

Dwaravati.description: Another name for Dwaraka, the city of Krishna.

Yadavas.description: The clan of Krishna, based in Dwaraka, descended from Yadu and including the Vrishnis.

Kinnari.description: A mythical being, half-woman and half-bird.

Vidyadhari.description: A female celestial being with magical powers.

Yakshi.description: A female nature spirit, sometimes benevolent or malevolent.

Kekaya.description: A kingdom in ancient India, maternal relatives of the Pandavas.

Sami tree.description: A sacred tree (Prosopis cineraria) where the Pandavas hide their weapons.

Yamuna.description: A major river in northern India, sacred in Hinduism.

Sami.description: A sacred tree (Prosopis cineraria) used to hide the Pandavas' weapons.

Yojana.description: An ancient unit of distance, roughly 8-9 miles.

Upaplavya.description: A city in the Matsya kingdom where the Pandavas stay after their incognito.

Muhurta.description: A unit of time, roughly 48 minutes.

Snataka.description: A graduate of Vedic studies, often a Brahmana who has completed his education.

Vina.description: A stringed musical instrument, similar to a lute.

Upadhana.description: A part of the Vina; here, a technical term in music.

Vedi.description: A sacrificial platform; also means 'wasp' in some contexts.

Vinda and Anuvinda.description: Princes of Avanti or the Kaikeyas who fought as allies of the Kauravas and were slain in battle.

Dhrishtaketu.description: The king of the Chedis and an ally of the Pandavas.

Ganga.description: The river goddess, mother of Bhishma, and a sacred river in Hindu mythology.

Amva.description: Daughters of the king of Kasi, whose lives are intertwined with Bhishma and Vichitravirya.

Hotravahana.description: A royal sage, maternal grandfather of Amva.

Akritavrana.description: A sage and companion of Parashurama.

Sthunakarna.description: A Yaksha who exchanges sexes with Sikhandini.

Hiranyavarman.description: The king of the Dasarnakas, father-in-law to Sikhandin.

Vatsabhumi.description: A region where Amva performed penance and became a river.

Prayaga.description: A sacred place of pilgrimage, the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers.

Bhogawati.description: A mythical city or region, sometimes associated with the Nagas.

Kampilya.description: The capital city of Drupada, king of Panchala.

Saubha.description: The city or kingdom ruled by Salwa.

Praswapa weapon.description: A celestial weapon capable of putting enemies to sleep, invoked by Bhishma.

Guhyaka.description: A class of semi-divine beings, attendants of Kubera.

Maharatha.description: A great chariot-warrior, able to fight thousands of opponents simultaneously.

Senamukha.description: A military unit, also called Gulma, consisting of a certain number of troops.

Pritana.description: A military unit larger than a Senamukha or Gulma.

Vahini.description: A large military division, composed of several Pritanas.

Dhwajini.description: Another term for a military division or unit.

Varuthini.description: Another term for a military division.

Prabhadrakas.description: A class or group of warriors allied with the Pandavas.

Srinjayas.description: A people or tribe allied with the Pandavas.

Praswapa.description: A celestial weapon that induces sleep or unconsciousness.

Samvodhana.description: A celestial weapon used to awaken someone put to sleep by the Praswapa weapon.

Yapa.description: A Vedic ritual or recitation of mantras.

Homa.description: A fire-sacrifice or ritual offering to the gods.

Pinda.description: A ritual offering of food to ancestors.

Tirtha.description: A sacred place of pilgrimage, often associated with water.

Ghatotkacha.description: Son of Bhima and the rakshasi Hidimbi, a powerful rakshasa warrior.

Radha.description: Foster mother of Karna, wife of Adhiratha.

Adhiratha.description: Karna's foster father, a charioteer by caste.

Bhagadatta.description: King of Pragjyotisha, renowned for his elephant warfare and fighting for the Kauravas.

Vrihadvala.description: King of Kosala, a Kaurava ally.

Sarvatobhadra.description: A type of battle array (vyuha) used in ancient Indian warfare, meaning 'safe on all sides.'

Makara.description: A battle formation named after the mythical sea creature (makara), resembling a crocodile or aquatic monster.

Vajra.description: A battle array named after the thunderbolt weapon of Indra; also refers to a diamond or thunderbolt.

Syena.description: A battle formation named after the hawk or eagle.

Sringataka.description: A battle array (vyuha) shaped like a horn or pointed formation.

Mandala.description: A circular battle array or formation.

Pragjyotisha.description: The kingdom ruled by Bhagadatta, known for its elephant forces.

Aindra weapon.description: A celestial weapon associated with Indra, the king of the gods.

Varuna weapon.description: A celestial weapon associated with Varuna, the god of water.

Vayavya weapon.description: A celestial weapon associated with the wind god Vayu.

Sataghni.description: A weapon resembling a spiked club or mace, used to kill many foes at once.

Kanka bird.description: A bird whose feathers are used for fletching arrows; often referenced in arrow descriptions.

Panchajanya.description: Krishna's conch, famous for its powerful sound.

Vaitarani.description: The mythical river separating the world of the living from the world of the dead.

Gayatri.description: A sacred Vedic meter and mantra, personified as a goddess.

Manasa lake.description: A sacred lake in the Himalayas, associated with the gods and sages.

Parjanya weapon.description: A celestial weapon associated with the rain god Parjanya, used to produce water or rain.

mantra.description: A sacred utterance, word, or phrase believed to have spiritual power.

Kshura.description: A type of arrowhead shaped like a razor.

nalika.description: A tubular arrow or sometimes a projectile weapon, possibly a kind of musket.

Sataghnis.description: A spiked weapon or missile designed to kill many foes at once.

chakra.description: A disc or wheel; in this context, a weapon (the discus of Vishnu/Krishna).

mace.description: A heavy club-like weapon, often with a spiked head.

conch.description: A shell used as a trumpet in battle and religious rituals.

standard.description: A flag or banner used to identify warriors or units on the battlefield.

leathern fence.description: A protective covering for the hand and arm used by archers.

calf-toothed arrow.description: An arrow with a head shaped like a calf's tooth, designed for piercing armor.

Brahma-danda.description: The staff or rod of a Brahmana, symbolizing spiritual authority and power.

Pramohana weapon.description: A celestial weapon that causes confusion or stupefaction.

Vritra.description: A demon slain by Indra in Vedic mythology, often representing drought or obstacles.

celestial weapon.description: A divine or supernatural weapon, often with magical properties, granted by gods.

Prishata.description: Father of Drupada, mentioned as the ancestor of Dhrishtadyumna.

Alayudha.description: A Rakshasa prince and enemy of the Pandavas, who is slain by Ghatotkacha.

Vrishasena.description: Son of Karna, a warrior who fights valiantly for the Kauravas.

Narayana weapon.description: A powerful celestial weapon invoked by Aswatthaman, capable of causing mass destruction and only pacified by laying down arms.

Brahma weapon.description: A supreme celestial weapon associated with the god Brahma, invoked by chanting specific mantras.

Pinaka.description: The bow of Lord Shiva (Mahadeva), symbolizing his power.

Phallic emblem.description: The lingam, a symbol of Shiva worshipped as the origin of the universe.

Sata Rudriya.description: A Vedic hymn in praise of Rudra (Shiva), recited for his blessings.

Praya.description: A vow of fasting unto death, often observed by warriors in extremis.

Sata-Rudriya.description: A hymn from the Vedas dedicated to Rudra (Shiva), recited for protection and blessings.

Samantapanchaka.description: A sacred region near Kurukshetra, associated with the Mahabharata war.

Kimpurushas.description: Mythical beings, half-man and half-horse, said to inhabit mountains.

Aksha.description: The axle or a measurement used for arrows as large as the axle of a chariot.

Sesha.description: The king of serpents and supporter of the world in Hindu cosmology, also known as Ananta.

Mandara.description: A sacred mountain, often used as a churning rod in Hindu mythology.

Prabhadraka.description: A special division or class of warriors, often associated with the Panchalas.

Nalika.description: A type of arrow or projectile, sometimes referring to a hollow or tube-like arrow.

Parigha.description: A heavy iron club or mace, often used as a weapon.

Mleccha.description: A term for foreigners or those outside the Vedic social order, often used for tribes considered barbaric.

Chandala.description: A person of the lowest caste, often associated with untouchability.

Samsaptaka.description: A warrior or group of warriors sworn to conquer or die, often used for a special division fighting Arjuna.

Shalya.description: The king of Madra and maternal uncle to Nakula and Sahadeva, a mighty warrior who fought for the Kauravas.

Ashvatthama.description: The son of Drona, a powerful and vengeful warrior fighting for the Kauravas, known for his mastery of celestial weapons and role in the night massacre.

Duhshasana.description: Duryodhana's brother, infamous for his role in Draupadi's humiliation; killed by Bhima.

Kritavarma.description: A chief of the Bhojas, Yadava warrior allied with the Kauravas, known for his prowess and loyalty.

Shakuni.description: The maternal uncle of Duryodhana and prince of Gandhara, a master of dice said to be an incarnation of the Dwapara Yuga.

Vaishampayana.description: A disciple of Vyasa and the narrator of the Mahabharata to King Janamejaya.

Uluka.description: Son of Shakuni, a Kaurava ally and messenger, who fights in the war.

Bhurishrava.description: A Kaurava ally, son of Somadatta, slain by Satyaki.

Bahlika.description: An elder Kuru prince and brother of Shantanu who remained a respected figure in the royal assembly.

Shantanu.description: Former king of Hastinapura, father of Bhishma.

Yuyutsu.description: A Kaurava prince who sides with the Pandavas.

Satyasena.description: A son of Karna, killed in the battle.

Sushena.description: Another son of Karna, killed in the battle.

Satyasandha.description: A son of Karna, mentioned among the survivors.

Ashvinis.description: The twin gods of medicine and health, fathers of Nakula and Sahadeva.

Bhava.description: The great god of the Hindu trinity, known by many names including Mahadeva and Sankara, and praised through the Sata-rudriya hymn.

Aswasena.description: A serpent (naga) whose mother was slain by Arjuna at Khandava, who enters Karna's arrow to seek revenge.

Brahma.description: The creator god, often called the Grandsire and identified with the deities Dhatri and Vidhatri.

Matali.description: The charioteer of Indra, mentioned as a comparison for Shalya.

Cedis.description: An allied kingdom of the Pandavas.

Kaikeyas.description: An allied kingdom of the Pandavas.

Yavanas.description: A term for western or foreign tribes, often Greeks or Central Asians.

Sakas.description: A northwestern tribe, often identified with the Scythians.

Vabhru.description: A prince of the Magadhas, allied with the Pandavas.

Satyajit.description: A Pandava ally, slain by Drona.

Yudhamanyu.description: A Panchala prince, protector of Arjuna's wheel.

Uttamauja.description: A Panchala prince, protector of Arjuna's wheel, and ally of the Pandavas, killed in the war.

Sutasoma.description: A son of Bhima, fighting for the Pandavas.

Srutakarman.description: A son of Arjuna, fighting for the Pandavas.

Srutakirti.description: A son of Sahadeva, fighting for the Pandavas.

Prativindhya.description: A son of Yudhishthira, fighting for the Pandavas.

Citra.description: A Kaurava prince, slain in battle.

Citravarman.description: A Kaurava prince, slain in battle.

Citrayudha.description: A Kaurava prince, slain in battle.

Citrayodhin.description: A Kaurava prince, slain in battle.

Anjalika.description: A type of powerful arrow; also refers to the specific arrow used by Arjuna to kill Karna.

Bhargava weapon.description: A powerful weapon given to Karna by Parashurama, also called the Bhargavastra.

Raudra weapon.description: A fierce celestial weapon associated with Rudra (Shiva).

Magadha.description: A powerful kingdom in eastern India, often involved in the war.

Kamboja.description: A northwestern kingdom or tribe, allied with the Kauravas.

Yavana.description: A term for western or foreign tribes, often Greeks or Central Asians.

Saka.description: A northwestern tribe, often identified with the Scythians.

Kulinda.description: A Himalayan tribe allied with the Pandavas.

astra.description: A celestial weapon, often invoked with mantras, possessing supernatural power.

maharatha.description: A great chariot-warrior, capable of fighting 720,000 opponents at once.

makara.description: A mythical sea creature, often depicted as a crocodile, used as a military formation shape.

bhargava.description: Descendant of Bhrigu; often refers to Parashurama.

mleccha.description: A term for non-Vedic or foreign peoples.

yuga.description: An epoch or era within Hindu cosmology.

ishta.description: Desired or chosen; often refers to a chosen deity.

Rishyasringa.description: A sage, his son fought in the war.

Pandya.description: A southern king, slain in battle.

Narayanas.description: Krishna's personal troops, some of whom fought for the Kauravas.

Gopalas.description: Cowherds, sometimes refers to Krishna's clan.

Shalya Parva.description: The ninth book of the Mahabharata, focusing on the events after Karna's death and the final battles.

Sarasvati.description: A sacred river and goddess of learning.

Sindhu.description: The Indus river or the region around it; a kingdom and its warriors, ruled by Jayadratha.

Matsyas.description: A kingdom allied with the Pandavas.

Satwata.description: A branch of the Yadava clan, including Satyaki and Kritavarma.

Kovidara.description: A type of tree, used as a standard on Dhrishtadyumna's chariot.

Dvaipayana lake.description: A lake where Duryodhana hides after the war.

mandala.description: A battle formation or a circular movement in mace fighting.

Parshni driver.description: A charioteer who drives the rear wheels or acts as an assistant to the main charioteer.

Shatanika.description: The son of Nakula and Draupadi.

Bhaga.description: A Vedic deity, whose eyes were plucked out by Shiva.

Parikshit.description: Grandson of Arjuna, sole surviving heir of the Pandavas.

Pushana.description: A Vedic deity, associated with nourishment.

Bhagiratha.description: A king who brought the Ganges to earth.

Satvata.description: A clan of the Yadavas, associated with Kritavarma.

Asta mountains.description: A mountain range where the sun is said to set.

Garuda.description: A mythical bird, vehicle of Vishnu, symbolizing speed and martial prowess.

gandiva.description: The celestial bow wielded by Arjuna.

praya.description: A vow of fasting unto death.

Kumara.description: Another name for Kartikeya, son of Shiva and Parvati.

bhushundis.description: A type of weapon, possibly a sling or missile.

shataghnis.description: Ancient weapons, possibly spiked clubs or projectiles.

mushalas.description: Maces or clubs used as weapons.

gomukha.description: A type of wind instrument, literally 'cow's mouth'.

jharjharas.description: A type of musical instrument, possibly cymbals.

Parvati.description: Consort of Shiva, goddess of power and fertility, also known as Uma and Gauri.

Shaibya.description: Name of a horse yoked to Krishna's chariot.

Sugriva.description: Name of a horse yoked to Krishna's chariot.

Meghapushpa.description: Name of a horse yoked to Krishna's chariot.

Balahaka.description: Name of a horse yoked to Krishna's chariot.

krita-yuga.description: The first of the four ages (yugas) in Hindu cosmology, the age of truth.

adamantine.description: Unbreakable or extremely hard, often used to describe armor or resolve.

car-warrior.description: A warrior who fights from a chariot.

libation.description: A ritual pouring of a liquid as an offering to a deity.

ascetic.description: A person who practices severe self-discipline and abstention.

homa.description: A Vedic fire ritual involving offerings to the fire.

vashat.description: A sacred exclamation used during Vedic rituals.

cubits.description: An ancient unit of length, roughly the length of a forearm.

regenerate.description: Born again, often used to refer to someone of high spiritual status.

preceptor.description: A teacher or instructor, especially in a spiritual or martial context.

coronal.description: Relating to a crown or the top of the head.

sire.description: A respectful term for a father or king.

wight.description: An archaic term for a person or creature.

sacrificial altar.description: A platform or structure used for making offerings in a ritual.

clarified butter.description: Also known as ghee, used in rituals and cooking.

sacrificial victim.description: The being or object offered in a sacrifice.

sacrificial fire.description: The fire into which offerings are made during rituals.

sacrificial offerings.description: Items offered to deities during a sacrifice.

Duhshala.description: Daughter of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, wife of Jayadratha.

Alambusha.description: A rakshasa (demon) warrior who fought for the Kauravas and was slain in battle.

Lomasa.description: A celestial sage who grants Yudhishthira the boon of spiritual vision.

Sudakshina.description: The king or prince of the Kambhojas who fought on the Kaurava side during the great war.

Pratipa.description: An ancestor of the Kuru dynasty.

Kshemadhanva.description: A king slain in the war.

Vrihanta.description: A king or warrior slain in the war.

Vrishaka.description: A warrior slain in the war.

Stri Parva.description: The Book of Women, the eleventh book of the Mahabharata, focusing on the lamentations of women after the war.

Jalapradanika-Parva.description: A sub-section of Stri Parva, dealing with the offering of water to the dead.

Brahman.description: The ultimate reality or universal spirit in Hindu philosophy.

Time.description: Personified as a cosmic force or deity that governs the fate and end of all beings.

Sindhu-Sauviras.description: Kingdoms in the northwest of ancient India, ruled by Jayadratha.

Madra.description: A kingdom in northwestern India, ruled by Shalya.

Kosalas.description: An ancient kingdom in northern India.

pitri-medha.description: Funeral rites performed for the deceased ancestors.

Uttara-Kurus.description: A mythical northern region, regarded as a land of the blessed.

Devapi.description: A sage and brother of Shantanu.

Skanda.description: The god of war, also known as Kartikeya.

Kalinga.description: An ancient kingdom in eastern India.

Brihadbala.description: King of Kosala, slain by Abhimanyu.

obsequial.description: Relating to funeral rites or ceremonies.

luminary.description: A celestial body or a person who inspires or influences others.

penances.description: Acts of self-mortification or devotion to express repentance or gain spiritual merit.

libations.description: Liquid offerings poured out as a religious ritual.

moksha.description: Liberation from the cycle of birth and death (samsara) in Hindu philosophy.

messengers of the Destroyer.description: A reference to the agents of Yama, the god of death.

Ordainer.description: A term for the divine force or god who ordains fate.

self-restraint.description: The practice of controlling one's desires and impulses.

renunciation.description: The act of giving up worldly pleasures and attachments.

heedfulness.description: The quality of being attentive or careful.

ascetic merit.description: Spiritual merit gained through austerities and self-discipline.

praya vow.description: A vow of fasting unto death, taken as a form of penance or protest.

angada.description: An armlet or bracelet, often worn by warriors.

keyura.description: An ornament worn on the upper arm.

cuirass.description: A piece of armor covering the body.

parijata.description: A celestial tree, here used metaphorically for a tree with flowery burden.

pitris.description: The spirits of ancestors in Hindu belief.

Suka.description: The son of Vyasa, a highly enlightened sage, renowned for his knowledge of the Vedas and his pursuit of Emancipation (Moksha).

Janaka.description: King of Mithila, renowned for his wisdom and devotion to the religion of Emancipation; often depicted as a philosopher-king.

Nara and Narayana.description: Twin sages, incarnations of the Supreme Deity, engaged in severe penances at Vadari; regarded as forms of Vishnu.

Saunaka.description: A sage and chief of the Naimisha forest conclave, to whom Sauti recites the Mahabharata.

Sauti.description: The narrator who recites the Mahabharata to the sages in Naimisha forest.

Padmanabha.description: A Naga chief, renowned for his righteousness and knowledge, whom a Brahmana seeks out for spiritual instruction.

Dharmaranya.description: A Brahmana who seeks instruction from the Naga Padmanabha regarding the highest religious duties.

Sankhya.description: A sage, regarded as the promulgator of the Sankhya philosophy.

Kapila.description: A great sage, considered the founder of the Sankhya system of philosophy.

Jaimini.description: A disciple of Vyasa, compiler of the Mimamsa Sutras.

Paila.description: A disciple of Vyasa, compiler of one of the Vedas.

Sumanta.description: A disciple of Vyasa, compiler of one of the Vedas.

Vrihaspati.description: The celestial preceptor of the gods and a sage associated with wisdom and ritual.

Madhu and Kaitabha.description: Two Asuras (demons) born from the primeval waters, slain by Narayana in his equine-headed form.

Sankhya and Yoga.description: Philosophical systems; Sankhya emphasizes knowledge and enumeration of principles, Yoga emphasizes meditation and union with the Supreme.

Vadari.description: A sacred retreat in the Himalayas, associated with the penances of Nara and Narayana.

White Island.description: A mystical realm in the northern ocean, inhabited by pure, awakened beings devoted to Narayana.

Meru.description: A mythological mountain considered the center of the universe in Hindu cosmology.

Gomati.description: A sacred river, on whose banks the Brahmana Dharmaranya waits for the Naga Padmanabha.

Pancharatra.description: A set of scriptures and a religious cult devoted to the worship of Narayana.

Mahabharata.description: The great epic composed by Vyasa, containing the Bhagavad Gita and numerous discourses on dharma.

Naimisha.description: A sacred forest where sages assemble and where the Mahabharata is recited.

Vaijayanta.description: A golden mountain in the midst of the Ocean of Milk, where Brahma meditates.

Sattwa, Rajas, Tamas.description: The three gunas or qualities of nature: purity, passion, and darkness.

Prakriti.description: Nature or the material cause of the universe, associated with the three gunas.

Purusha.description: The Supreme Person or Soul, the conscious principle in the universe.

Kshetrajna.description: The knower of the field, i.e., the soul that perceives and experiences.

Kshetra.description: The field, i.e., the body or the aggregate of material principles.

Sattwata.description: A cult or ritual system associated with the worship of Narayana.

Sankhya-Yoga.description: The combined philosophical system of Sankhya (knowledge) and Yoga (practice).

Goloka.description: A region of supreme felicity, associated with Krishna and the gopis.

Pradhana.description: The unmanifest principle, or primordial matter, in Sankhya philosophy.

Mahat.description: The great principle, or cosmic intelligence, in Sankhya philosophy.

Ahankara.description: The principle of egoism or self-consciousness in Sankhya philosophy.

Tattwa.description: A principle or element; in Sankhya, one of the categories of existence.

Pravritti.description: The path of action, or engagement in worldly duties.

Nivritti.description: The path of renunciation or abstention from worldly acts.

Ekanta.description: The religion of exclusive devotion to Narayana.

Hari-Gita.description: Another name for the Bhagavad Gita, the discourse of Krishna to Arjuna.

Yoga.description: A system of philosophy and practice aiming at union with the Supreme Soul through meditation and self-restraint.

Unccha.description: A vow or mode of living by subsisting on gleaned grains left in the fields after harvest.

Dharana.description: Concentration of the mind on a single object, a stage in Yoga practice.

Samadhi.description: A state of deep meditative absorption in Yoga, leading to union with the Supreme.

Gunas.description: The three qualities of nature: Sattwa (purity), Rajas (passion), and Tamas (darkness).

Sattwa.description: The quality of purity, light, and harmony.

Rajas.description: The quality of passion, activity, and restlessness.

Tamas.description: The quality of darkness, inertia, and ignorance.

Smriti.description: Tradition; texts regarded as remembered, such as the Dharma-shastras.

Kalpa.description: A day of Brahma, a vast period of time in Hindu cosmology.

Pratyahara.description: Withdrawal of the senses from their objects, a stage in Yoga.

Vasana.description: Desire or impression left by past actions.

Vedanta.description: The end or culmination of the Vedas; the philosophical teachings of the Upanishads.

Jiva.description: The individual soul or living being.

Atman.description: The Self or soul, identical with Brahman in Vedanta.

Durvasa.description: A powerful and irascible sage considered an incarnation of Shiva, born as the son of the rishi Atri.

Sachi.description: Wife of Indra, the king of the gods.

Atri.description: A great rishi and one of the Saptarishis, father of Dattatreya; 'Atri's son' refers to Durvasa.

Utathya.description: A powerful Brahmana sage, husband of Bhadra, who demonstrated the might of Brahmanas.

Kasyapa.description: A sage and progenitor, regarded as a Brahmana and father of many creatures.

Sura.description: Ancestor in Krishna's lineage, father of Vasudeva.

Bhadra.description: Daughter of Soma, wife of Utathya.

Dhanin.description: Messenger of the Kapas, sent to parley with the Brahmanas.

Kapas.description: A virtuous race of beings, destroyed by the Brahmanas in a cosmic conflict.

Mada.description: A terrible Asura created by Chyavana to compel Indra to let the Ashwins drink Soma.

Sata-rudriya.description: A hymn of a thousand names and attributes of Rudra/Shiva, recited for merit and protection.

Savitra.description: A Vedic deity associated with the sun and with the sacred Gayatri mantra.

Rathantara.description: A particular Saman (melodic hymn) in the Sama Veda, used in rituals.

Krittikas.description: The Pleiades, a group of stars; in mythology, the six mothers who nursed Kartikeya.

Kumbhipaka.description: A hell in Hindu cosmology where sinners are cooked in boiling oil.

Kausiki.description: A sacred river, also known as the Kosi.

Savitri Mantras.description: Sacred Vedic hymns, especially the Gayatri, recited for spiritual merit.

Vishwaksena.description: A name of Vishnu, meaning 'he whose army is the universe.'

Govardhana.description: A sacred hill lifted by Krishna to protect the cowherds from Indra's wrath.

Sankalpa.description: A solemn vow or resolution, often made before a ritual.

Diksha.description: Initiation or consecration into a religious vow or practice.

Vighasa.description: The food that remains after serving gods, guests, and dependents; what a householder should eat.

Vihita.description: Prescribed or enjoined by scripture or authority.

Nishkama.description: Action performed without desire for its fruits; selfless action.

Sakama.description: Action performed with desire for its fruits; motivated action.

Kundasin.description: A pander or one who lives by arranging sexual liaisons for others.

Upadhyaya.description: A teacher, especially one who instructs in the Vedas.

Acharya.description: A preceptor or teacher, often one who teaches all the Vedas.

Vrata.description: A religious vow or observance, often involving fasting or special practices.

Upavasa.description: Fasting or abstention from food, often as a religious observance.

Samyava.description: A kind of thin cake made of flour, fried with ghee.

Krisara.description: A kind of liquid food made of rice, sesame, milk, and spices.

Payasa.description: Rice boiled in milk and sugar; a sweet dish offered in rituals.

Agama.description: Scriptural tradition or authoritative text, often referring to scriptures outside the Vedas.

Sudarsana.description: The divine discus (chakra) wielded by Vishnu/Krishna.

Marutta.description: Ancient king celebrated for his great sacrifice and immense wealth.

Samvarta.description: A sage, younger brother of Vrihaspati, who officiated at Marutta's sacrifice.

Saryati.description: A king mentioned in connection with the sage Chyavana.

Vasistha.description: A revered sage, one of the Saptarishis, and family priest to the Kuru dynasty.

Satyaka.description: A Vrishni hero, companion of Krishna.

Chitrangada.description: Princess of Manipura, wife of Arjuna, and mother of Vabhruvahana.

Vabhruvahana.description: Son of Arjuna and Chitrangada, ruler of Manipura.

Vajradatta.description: Son of Bhagadatta, king of Pragjyotisha, who fought Arjuna during the horse-sacrifice.

Suryavarman.description: King of the Trigartas, who opposed Arjuna during the horse-sacrifice.

Ketuvarman.description: Younger brother of Suryavarman, slain by Arjuna.

Dhritavarman.description: A Trigarta prince who fought Arjuna.

Meghasandhi.description: Prince of Magadha who fought Arjuna during the horse-sacrifice.

Sarabha.description: Son of Sisupala, ruler of the Chedis.

Ekalavya.description: Nishada prince and archer, whose son fought Arjuna.

Rantideva.description: King renowned for his generosity and gift of water.

Nriga.description: King who fell into hell for giving away a cow that did not belong to him.

Mongoose.description: A mysterious, half-golden mongoose who appears at Yudhishthira's horse-sacrifice to teach a lesson about true merit.

Sarvamedha.description: A Vedic sacrifice involving the offering of all things.

Naramedha.description: A human sacrifice, mentioned as an ancient practice.

Dakshina.description: The sacrificial fee or gift given to priests at the conclusion of a sacrifice.

Karandhama.description: An ancient royal race or dynasty, ancestors of Marutta.

Angira.description: A sage, father of Vrihaspati and Samvarta.

Jyoti.description: Luminous matter or light, one of the five elements.

Akasa.description: The element of ether or space.

Anarttas.description: A people or region associated with Krishna's kingdom.

Dhruba.description: A constellation, possibly referring to the Pole Star.

Chaitra.description: A month in the Hindu lunar calendar.

Sphya.description: A wooden sword or scimitar used in sacrifice.

Kurcha.description: A handful of Kusa grass used in rituals.

Nishada.description: A tribal people, Ekalavya's lineage; often forest-dwellers.

Gokarna.description: A sacred place on the western coast of India.

Jamvudwipa.description: The central continent in ancient Indian cosmology.

Vasu.description: A group of deities, also refers to King Vasu.

Saktu.description: Barley meal or flour, often used as food or offering.

Pravargya.description: A preliminary rite in a Vedic sacrifice.

Chayana.description: The altar or mound built for a Vedic sacrifice.

Vilwa.description: A type of tree (Aegle marmelos) used in sacrifices.

Khadira.description: A type of tree (Acacia catechu) used in sacrifices.

Devadaru.description: A type of tree (Himalayan cedar) used in sacrifices.

Sleshmataka.description: A type of tree (Cordia latifolia) used in sacrifices.

Palasa.description: A type of tree (Butea frondosa) used in sacrifices.

Khandavaraga.description: A sweetmeat made of piper longum, ginger, and mung bean juice.

parva.description: Book or section of the Mahabharata.

prastha.description: A measure of volume, about four Kudavas.

achamana.description: A ritual act of sipping water for purification before a rite.

charu.description: A kind of food offering made of rice, milk, and sugar.

putra.description: A son; literally 'one who saves from hell (put).'

Jarasandha.description: King of Magadha, a powerful enemy of the Pandavas, slain by Bhima.

Suvala.description: Father of Gandhari, king of Gandhara.

Vichitraviryya.description: Father of Dhritarashtra and Pandu, former king of Hastinapura.

Satayupa.description: A royal sage, former king of the Kekayas, who retired to the forest.

Parvata.description: A sage, often mentioned with Narada.

Devala.description: A sage, contemporary of Narada and Parvata.

Sringin.description: Son of the sage Samika, known for cursing Parikshit.

Astika.description: A sage who stops Janamejaya's snake sacrifice.

Mandavya.description: A sage who cursed Dharma to be born as Vidura.

Vasus.description: A group of eight deities; Bhishma is an incarnation of one.

Sala.description: A warrior slain in the war.

Achala.description: A warrior slain in the war.

Prishadhra.description: A king mentioned as attaining heaven through penance.

Purukutsa.description: A king who attained heaven through penance.

Sasaloman.description: A king who attained heaven through penance.

Sahasrachitya.description: A king, grandfather of Satayupa, who attained heaven through penance.

Sailalaya.description: Grandfather of Bhagadatta, attained heaven through penance.

Kuru-jangala.description: A region in the Kuru kingdom.

Gangadwara.description: A sacred place at the source of the Ganges, modern Haridwar.

Yayavaras.description: A Brahmin lineage; Astika belongs to this lineage.

Narmada.description: A sacred river in central India.

Sukra.description: The preceptor of the Asuras and a sage of great wisdom, also known as Usanas.

Asramavasika Parva.description: The fifteenth book of the Mahabharata, focusing on the retirement of Dhritarashtra and others to the forest.

Earth.description: Personified as a goddess in Hindu mythology; here refers to the land ruled by the kings.

Karu's race.description: Refers to the descendants of Kuru.

Vaisyas.description: The merchant and agricultural class in Hindu society.

Sudras.description: The laborer and servant class in Hindu society.

Kuru kingdom.description: The territory ruled by the Kuru dynasty, centered on Hastinapura.

Kuru king.description: Refers to the reigning king of the Kuru dynasty.

Maireya wines.description: A type of wine mentioned in ancient texts.

Phaseolus Mango.description: A plant, possibly referring to a type of bean or pulse.

Aralikas.description: Cooks specializing in preparing potherbs cut with a specific tool.

Ragakhandava.description: A preparation made from piper longum, dry ginger, sugar, and the juice of Phaseolus Mango.

Sapindikarana.description: A specific Sraddha ritual performed a year after death to unite the departed with the ancestors.

Mahadana.description: Great gifts such as elephants, horses, or land, given in charity.

Atatayins.description: Six types of heinous criminals in Hindu law, including arsonists and poisoners.

Sakata.description: A military formation shaped like a cart.

mahadana.description: Great gifts such as elephants, horses, or land, given in charity.

preta.description: A departed spirit or ghost, especially before the completion of funeral rites.

guna.description: A quality or attribute; refers to the three fundamental qualities—sattwa, rajas, tamas.

parvan.description: A book or section of the Mahabharata.

kutha.description: A blanket or rug, often made from animal skin.

Vishvamitra.description: A revered sage (rishi) in Hindu tradition.

Kanwa.description: A sage (rishi) in Hindu mythology, known for his wisdom.

Jara.description: The hunter who accidentally kills Krishna with an arrow.

Ahuka.description: A king of the Vrishnis, sometimes identified with Ugrasena, grandfather of Krishna.

Satrajit.description: Father of Satyabhama and owner of the Syamantaka gem.

Charudeshna.description: A son of Krishna, slain in the carnage.

Aniruddha.description: Grandson of Krishna, son of Pradyumna.

Anakadundubhi.description: The father of Krishna and a chief of the Vrishnis, also known by the name Anakadundubhi.

Haimavati.description: A wife of Krishna, mentioned among those who ascend the funeral pyre.

Jamvabati.description: A wife of Krishna, daughter of the bear-king Jambavan.

Kukuras.description: A clan related to the Yadavas, destroyed in the carnage.

Adityas.description: A group of solar deities, sons of Aditi.

Viswedevas.description: A group of universal deities in Vedic tradition.

Siddhas.description: Perfected beings, often of semi-divine status.

Prithusravas.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Kunjara.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Misri.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Sankha.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Kumuda.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Hrada.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Kratha.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Chakramanda.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Atishanda.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Amvarisha.description: A naga mentioned among those receiving Balarama.

Chaidya.description: Refers to Shishupala, king of Chedi, slain by Krishna.

Kalingas.description: A people and kingdom in eastern India.

Saranga.description: The celestial bow wielded by Krishna.

Brahmana’s rod of chastisement.description: A metaphor for the curse or punishment delivered by Brahmin sages.

Eraka grass.description: A type of grass that, due to the curse, turned into iron bolts during the carnage.

Rahu.description: A celestial demon who causes eclipses by swallowing the sun or moon.

Syamantaka.description: A legendary gem associated with Krishna and Satrajit.

Shakraprastha.description: A city where Vajra, Krishna’s grandson, was established as king.

Marttikavat.description: A city where the son of Kritavarma and the Bhoja women were settled.

Valahaka.description: A horse, one of the four steeds of Krishna’s chariot.

viands.description: An archaic English word for food or provisions.

lunation.description: A lunar month; the period between two new moons.

concourse.description: A large gathering or assembly of people.

impaled.description: A form of execution or punishment where a person is pierced with a stake.

Yajnavalkya.description: A revered sage of the Bharadwaja lineage.

Maruts.description: A group of storm deities in Hindu mythology.

Dwaita.description: A forest where the Pandavas spent part of their exile.

Daityas.description: A race of powerful demons, often opposed by the gods.

Krodhavasas.description: Mythical beings who take away the merit of sacrifices seen by dogs.

Renunciation.description: The act of giving up worldly life and attachments for spiritual pursuit.

sacred fires.description: Vedic household fires maintained for rituals and worship, symbolizing domestic and religious duties.

Sadhyas.description: A class of celestial beings or deities associated with righteousness and worship.

Nishatha.description: A son of Madri, sometimes listed among the sons of Pandavas.

Bhanukampa.description: A character associated with the Yadava lineage.

Viduratha.description: A warrior mentioned among those who attained Heaven.

Bhuri.description: A warrior mentioned among those who attained Heaven.

Varchas.description: A celestial being, son of Soma, incarnated as Abhimanyu.

Dushmanta.description: An ancient king, ancestor of the Bharata dynasty.

Hariscandra.description: A legendary king renowned for his truthfulness.

Mandhatri.description: A legendary king of great renown.

Svargarohanika Parva.description: The eighteenth and final book of the Mahabharata, describing the ascent to Heaven.

Kuta-salmalika.description: A mythical tree with sharp thorns, associated with hellish punishments.

Rudras.description: A group of storm deities, associated with Shiva.

Angirasa.description: A sage, ancestor of Drona through Brihaspati.

Takshasila.description: An ancient city, also known as Taxila, a center of learning.

Sankhya Yoga.description: A philosophical system and spiritual discipline in Hinduism.

Astika-parva.description: The first book of the Mahabharata, recounting the story of Astika.

Sabha-parva.description: The second book of the Mahabharata, describing the royal court.

Aranyaka-parva.description: The 'Book of the Forest,' the third book of the Mahabharata, detailing the Pandavas' exile.

Virata-parva.description: The fourth book, describing the Pandavas' incognito year.

Udyoga-parva.description: The fifth book, detailing the preparations for war.

Bhishma-parva.description: The sixth book, focusing on the battle under Bhishma's command.

Drona-parva.description: The seventh book, focusing on the battle under Drona's command.

Karna-parva.description: The eighth book, focusing on the battle under Karna's command.

Gada-parva.description: The tenth book, describing the mace battle between Bhima and Duryodhana.

Stri-parva.description: The eleventh book, focusing on the lament of the women after the war.

Shanti-parva.description: The twelfth book, containing discourses on peace and duty.

Asvamedhika-parva.description: The Book of the Horse-sacrifice, the 14th book of the Mahabharata, describing Yudhishthira's horse-sacrifice.

Mausala.description: The sixteenth book, describing the destruction of the Yadava clan.

Mahaprasthanika.description: The seventeenth book, describing the Pandavas' final journey.

Svarga-parva.description: The eighteenth book, describing the Pandavas' ascent to Heaven.

Harivansa.description: An appendix to the Mahabharata, detailing the genealogy of Krishna.

Agnishtoma.description: A Vedic sacrifice, considered the basic Soma ritual.

Atiratra.description: A Vedic ritual extending over a night, considered highly meritorious.

Dwadasaha.description: A Vedic sacrifice lasting twelve days.

Vajapeya.description: A Vedic sacrifice associated with kingship and power.

Horse-sacrifice.description: Also called Ashvamedha, a royal ritual for sovereignty.

Kailasa.description: A sacred mountain, abode of Shiva.

Kapila cow.description: A sacred brown or reddish cow, considered highly auspicious as a gift.

ordinances.description: Prescribed rules or laws, especially in a religious context.

veritable.description: True or real; used to emphasize the aptness of a description.

fraught.description: Filled with or destined to result in (something undesirable).

behoveth.description: It is necessary or proper (archaic English).

scorcher of foes.description: An epithet meaning a powerful warrior who destroys enemies.

noisome.description: Having an extremely offensive smell; unpleasant.

fastnesses.description: Strongholds or secure places, often difficult to access.

denizens.description: Inhabitants or occupants of a particular place.

scimitar.description: A curved, single-edged sword of Eastern origin.

benedictions.description: Blessings or expressions of good wishes.

frumenty.description: A dish made of hulled wheat boiled in milk, often sweetened.

havisya.description: Food suitable for offering in a Vedic sacrifice, usually simple and pure.

apupas.description: A type of cake or sweet made from flour, used in rituals.

pupas.description: Another type of ritual cake or sweet.

modakas.description: Sweet dumplings, often offered to deities.

Nupuras.description: Anklets, especially those with bells, worn by women.

Parana.description: A section or reading session of a sacred text.

Dwadasaha vow.description: A Vedic ritual lasting twelve days.

Vajapeya sacrifice.description: A Vedic ritual associated with kingship and power.

Rajasuya sacrifice.description: A royal consecration ritual performed by ancient Indian kings.

Brahmanicide.description: The act of killing a Brahmana, considered a grave sin.

Savittri.description: A sacred hymn or verse, often recited for spiritual merit.

Krishna.description: The central figure of the Mahabharata and an incarnation of Vishnu, also known by numerous epithets including Acyuta, Hari, and Narayana.

Yudhishthira.description: The eldest of the five Pandava brothers and the righteous king who rules Hastinapura after the Kurukshetra War. Known as Dharmaraja for his unwavering commitment to truth and justice.
